CDK5-dependent NUP98 phosphorylation initiates nuclear-import failure in TARDBP-mutant motor neurons

Hypothesis. In human motor neurons carrying an ALS-associated TARDBP mutation, excessive CDK5-dependent phosphorylation of pore-associated NUP98 initiates nuclear-import failure before persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies appear. The proposed modification reduces NUP98 retention at nuclear pores, compromising import and depleting nuclear TDP-43. Subsequent cytoplasmic TDP-43 accumulation amplifies transport disruption and contributes to neuronal dysfunction. This is a proposed proximal initiating mechanism in a defined ALS context, not a universal explanation of ALS.

Supported premises. Disease-linked TDP-43 can disrupt nucleoporin localization and nucleocytoplasmic transport, and pore pathology occurs in ALS tissue [S1]. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can accompany transport-factor mislocalization, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death without conventional stress granules [S3]. Cellular stress can also recruit transport factors into stress granules and impair transport [S4]. These findings support transport dysfunction as a relevant phenotype but leave its initiating lesion unresolved. Phosphorylated TDP-43 in S3 is not evidence of phosphorylated NUP98. C9orf72-repeat-associated RanGAP mislocalization supplies a distinct, genotype-specific route to impaired import [S2]; it does not validate the proposed TARDBP mechanism.

Speculative bridges. Candidate selection—NUP98 as a nucleoporin and CDK5 as a kinase—uses unverified prior knowledge. Their proposed coupling in ALS is an assumption. Neither direct CDK5 phosphorylation of NUP98, phosphorylation-dependent loss of pore residence, nor precedence over TDP-43 pathology is established by this packet. The relevant residue is deliberately unspecified: identifying a reproducible, disease-associated, CDK5-dependent NUP98 phosphosite is a prerequisite, not permission to substitute another nucleoporin after a negative result. The downstream feedback from import failure to persistent TDP-43 assemblies is also speculative.

Discriminating preclinical strategy. Study independently derived TARDBP-mutant induced-pluripotent-stem-cell motor-neuron lines alongside their isogenic corrected controls, using matched differentiation and maturation conditions. Begin measurements before detectable persistent TDP-43 assemblies. Combine quantitative NUP98 phosphosite analysis, normalized to total NUP98 abundance, with pore-localization imaging, nuclear-import kinetics, nuclear TDP-43 abundance, cytoplasmic assemblies, stress-granule formation, and neuronal survival. Measure export, passive permeability, and general cellular stress separately so that altered reporter localization is not automatically interpreted as defective import. Prespecify sustained reduction in import rate as the primary functional endpoint; TDP-43 redistribution and survival are secondary outcomes.

First, establish whether a NUP98 phosphosite increases before import failure, is reduced by acute genetic CDK5 suppression, and can be generated by active—but not catalytically inactive—CDK5 in a purified biochemical assay. These results would support direct substrate assignment, although the biochemical assay alone would not establish cellular causality. Next, introduce an endogenous phosphorylation-resistant substitution at the mapped site, with independently generated clones and a sequence-reverted control. Confirm that the substitution preserves baseline NUP98 abundance, pore localization, and transport in corrected neurons. The hypothesis predicts that blocking this modification delays import failure and nuclear TDP-43 depletion despite continued expression of mutant TARDBP. CDK5 suppression should provide little additional protection once the relevant NUP98 phosphorylation is blocked.

Alternatives and discrimination. An alternative is that TDP-43 assemblies or stress granules first sequester transport factors, with NUP98 phosphorylation arising secondarily [S1, S3, S4]. Broader cellular stress could also drive both measurements without a causal link. Independently attenuate conventional stress-granule assembly and persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly formation, verifying their effects rather than assuming specificity. Compare these perturbations factorially with the NUP98 substitution. Protection by NUP98 blockade before assemblies emerge would favor an intrinsic pore lesion; protection only through assembly suppression, followed by normalization of phosphorylation, would favor a downstream response. Stress-granule inhibition alone cannot exclude the granule-independent alternative supported by S3.

Falsification and limitations. The initiating hypothesis would be falsified if verified blockade of the mapped NUP98 phosphorylation preserves baseline pore function yet leaves the earliest import defect and nuclear TDP-43 loss unchanged, while assembly suppression prevents those defects. Failure to identify a disease-associated direct CDK5-dependent site would also reject this specified mechanism. Temporal ordering alone is insufficient, substitutions may alter protein structure independently of phosphorylation, and kinase perturbations may affect other substrates. Cultured-neuron results would not establish clinical causation or generalization across ALS genotypes.

Hypothesis title: Phosphorylation of NUP98 initiates nuclear-import failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy models of ALS.

This proposal tests one claim: in experimental TDP-43 proteinopathy, phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin NUP98 is an initiating nuclear-pore alteration that impairs selective nuclear import and thereby promotes nuclear TDP-43 depletion and neuronal dysfunction. The initiating event is the covalent pore modification. Nuclear TDP-43 loss, cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly, and cell death are treated as downstream responses. The claim is limited to TDP-43 proteinopathy models and TDP-43-positive ALS tissue, and is not offered as a single route for every genetic or sporadic ALS subtype.

Supported premises. Disease-linked TDP-43 associates with insoluble nuclear-pore and transport components, disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in cell systems, and accompanies pore pathology in ALS tissue [S1]. These findings support a causal study of pore alteration in TDP-43 proteinopathy. They leave the initiating chemistry and the sequence across ALS subtypes unspecified [S1]. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form independently of conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport-associated proteins, and coincide with impaired import, loss of nuclear TDP-43, and cell death [S3]. Phosphorylated TDP-43 inside those assemblies is a modification of TDP-43 and is separate from nucleoporin phosphorylation [S3]. Expanded C9orf72 RNA is linked to RanGAP mislocalization and impaired import in that genetic context, and transport-directed manipulations can modify model phenotypes [S2]. Cellular stress can recruit transport factors into stress granules and impair transport, and changing stress-granule assembly can modify those defects [S4]. Together, [S3] and [S4] show that more than one upstream route can produce transport failure.

Speculative bridges. The choice of NUP98, the kinase, and the phospho-acceptor sites are assumptions. Unverified prior knowledge holds that mitotic CDK1 phosphorylation of FG-nucleoporins, including NUP98, loosens the selective barrier during nuclear-envelope breakdown. The bridge assumed here is that a proline-directed kinase, provisionally a CDK-family enzyme, writes an analogous mark on NUP98 in post-mitotic neurons during TDP-43 proteinopathy, and that this mark slows importin-mediated cargo entry before stress granules sequester transport factors and before insoluble TDP-43 accumulates. A further speculative bridge reads the nucleoporin mislocalization in [S1] as possible phospho-dependent release of NUP98 from the pore. No supplied source establishes that kinase, those sites, or that order.

Alternative explanations. Transport factors may be sequestered in stress granules so that import fails while the pore remains covalently intact [S4]. Cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing may inhibit import directly, placing any pore change downstream [S3]. TDP-43 aggregates may displace nucleoporins, so later phosphorylation would mark damaged pores [S1]. In C9orf72 models, repeat RNA and RanGAP mislocalization may explain import failure without NUP98 phosphorylation [S2]. Import failure may also follow broader energetic or proteotoxic stress.

Discriminating preclinical test. In human iPSC-derived motor neurons with inducible disease-linked TDP-43, and in a matched stress paradigm that assembles stress granules without mutant TDP-43, collect a time series of NPC-enriched NUP98 phosphorylation, a quantitative nuclear-import reporter, G3BP1-positive stress granules, and the nuclear-to-cytoplasmic TDP-43 ratio. The hypothesis predicts a rise in NUP98 phosphorylation before the import reporter declines, including when stress-granule assembly is prevented. Endogenous NUP98 is then replaced, at near-endogenous levels, by a phosphorylation-resistant variant or a phosphorylation-mimetic variant at the candidate proline-directed sites. The hypothesis predicts that the resistant variant preserves import, nuclear TDP-43, and survival when stress granules form or when cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies are already present, whereas the mimetic variant impairs import in otherwise healthy neurons. A crossed arm blocks stress-granule assembly while NUP98 phospho-status is measured independently. The same phosphorylation assay is applied to C9orf72-repeat neurons to test whether a RanGAP-linked import defect [S2] depends on NUP98 phosphorylation.

Falsifying observation. The hypothesis is falsified if import failure and neuronal death keep the same timing and severity when NUP98 cannot be phosphorylated at the candidate sites, or if NUP98 phosphorylation is detected only after import has already failed and after nucleoporins are already mislocalized with insoluble TDP-43. It is also falsified if phosphorylation-mimetic NUP98 leaves import intact in healthy neurons, or if blocking stress-granule assembly restores import while NUP98 remains phosphorylated, an outcome that would favor sequestration [S4] in that model.

Limitations. Kinase identity, sites, and the selection of NUP98 lie outside [S1]–[S4]. Phosphomimetic substitutions only approximate phosphate. Phosphorylation of other nucleoporins could still matter if this NUP98-site claim fails. iPSC-neuron timing may differ from human disease chronology. The design tests a research hypothesis and does not validate a treatment.

HYPOTHESIS TITLE: Stress-activated kinase hyperphosphorylation of nuclear-pore Nup98 as an initiating, pore-intrinsic cause of nuclear-import failure in TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS.

PROPOSED MECHANISM (causal chain): In ALS contexts driven by TDP-43 proteinopathy (sporadic ALS with TDP-43 inclusions and C9orf72 expansion carriers), persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies and/or repeat-RNA-associated stress activate one or more stress-responsive kinases in motor neurons. These kinases hyperphosphorylate the intrinsically disordered, FG/GLFG-rich N-terminal region of the nucleoporin Nup98 at the pore. Phosphorylation reduces Nup98 residence on the pore scaffold and its barrier-forming capacity, weakening Ran-gated selectivity; nuclear import fails, nuclear TDP-43 is depleted, cytoplasmic aggregation accelerates, and a feed-forward loop leads to neuronal dysfunction and death. The initiating event is proposed to be the covalent pore modification; transport-factor sequestration, stress-granule assembly, and nuclear TDP-43 loss are treated as downstream or parallel responses.

SUPPORTED PREMISES (packet evidence only):
- S1: TDP-43 aggregates associate with nuclear-pore and transport components, and disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and import in experimental systems, with pore pathology in ALS tissue. This establishes that pore disruption accompanies TDP-43 pathology, but not any nucleoporin phosphorylation event.
- S2: C9orf72 repeat RNA alters RanGAP localization and impairs import in models and patient-derived neurons, making transport dysfunction a convergent phenotype across at least two ALS-related contexts.
- S3: Cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing independent of stress granules impairs import, depletes nuclear TDP-43, and causes cell death; phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulates in these assemblies. This shows phosphorylation marks pathological assemblies — of TDP-43 itself, not nucleoporins.
- S4: Stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs transport, and perturbing granule assembly modifies phenotypes. This defines the principal sequestration-based alternative and a perturbational logic to emulate. S1–S2 caution against universal mechanisms, so the hypothesis is scoped to TDP-43-proteinopathy/C9orf72 contexts.

SPECULATIVE BRIDGES (explicitly labeled assumptions):
1. Target and site: Nup98 is assumed to carry disease-relevant phosphorylation in its FG/GLFG-rich disordered region. Unverified prior knowledge (not in the packet): FG nucleoporins such as Nup98 undergo mitotic phospho-regulation of pore disassembly and barrier properties; whether analogous stress-triggered phosphorylation occurs in aging motor neurons is untested.
2. Kinase identity: unknown; candidate kinases are explicitly an assumption to be identified by screening.
3. Temporal precedence: phosphorylation precedes measurable import failure — this is the core hypothesis claim to be tested, not evidence.

ALTERNATIVE EXPLANATIONS:
- A1 (S3/S4): import failure results from sequestration of RanGAP/karyopherins in stress granules or TDP-43 condensates; nucleoporin phosphorylation is a bystander stress response.
- A2 (S1): aggregates physically displace or mislocalize nucleoporins without covalent modification.
- A3: phosphorylation reflects generic cell-death/energy stress secondary to broader collapse.

DISCRIMINATING PRECLINICAL TEST STRATEGY:
- Models: (a) human iPSC-derived motor neurons with inducible cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly formation (S3-like); (b) C9orf72-expansion patient iPSC motor neurons with isogenic corrected controls (S2-like).
- Time-resolved sampling before overt toxicity, measuring concurrently: Nup98 (plus comparison Nups such as Nup62 and Nup153) phosphosite occupancy in enriched pore fractions by targeted LC-MS/MS, with phospho-Nup98 immunostaining validated by phosphatase and phosphopeptide-competition controls; functional NLS-GFP import kinetics and Ran-gradient integrity; sequestration readouts (soluble fraction of karyopherin-beta1 and RanGAP, poly(A)+ RNA export, G3BP1 stress-granule imaging per the S4 contrast); nuclear TDP-43; cell viability.
- Causal manipulations: CRISPR-based endogenous phospho-null editing (Ser/Thr-to-Ala) of mapped Nup98 sites versus phosphomimetic (Ser-to-Asp) replacement at endogenous-like expression levels; kinase identification via phosphoproteomic motif analysis and a CRISPRi kinase screen, followed by kinase-dead or inhibitor perturbation.
- Discrimination criteria: the initiating mechanism requires (1) phosphorylation onset statistically preceding import decline; (2) phospho-null Nup98 preserving import and delaying nuclear TDP-43 loss even when transport-factor sequestration still occurs; (3) phosphomimetic Nup98 alone, without TDP-43 aggregation or stress granules, being sufficient to impair import. If sequestration appears first and pore phospho-edits have no effect, alternative A1 is favored.

FALSIFYING OBSERVATION: In inducible TDP-43 motor neurons, NLS-GFP import falls within about 12 hours of induction while Nup98 phosphorylation shows no rise above baseline at or before onset; endogenous phospho-null Nup98 editors fail to rescue import, nuclear TDP-43, or survival; and phosphomimetic Nup98 produces no transport phenotype. Together these would falsify the initiating-pore-phosphorylation hypothesis and support sequestration-based mechanisms (S3/S4), placing phosphorylation firmly downstream.

LIMITATIONS: Phosphosite occupancy and kinase identity may be hard to resolve near onset; iPSC motor neurons are developmentally immature and may miss adult-onset biology; editing Nup98 can itself perturb pore integrity and viability, requiring careful expression-matched designs; kinase redundancy and compensation may blunt perturbations; and the hypothesis is scoped to TDP-43-proteinopathy/C9orf72 ALS and does not claim generality across subtypes (e.g., SOD1-like models remain untested). Success in this assay would establish a testable initiating mechanism, not a validated treatment target.

Endogenous cleavage-resistant p35 and genetic CDK5 suppression must prevent it; purified active, but not kinase-dead, CDK5–p25 must phosphorylate the same sites.

Causal tests. Use inducible, endogenous-dose phospho-null NUP98 replacement before onset, with sequence-reverted controls; verify abundance, pore incorporation, baseline transport, and removal of mapped phosphorylation while upstream calcium/CDK5 activation remains matched. For sufficiency, acutely recruit active CDK5–p25 to endogenously tagged NUP98 in corrected neurons, reproducing disease-level site occupancy. Actual phosphorylation must promptly reproduce permeability/import defects with wild-type but not phospho-null NUP98; include kinase-dead and no-recruitment controls. Monitor NUP62/NUP153 phosphorylation and localization; emerging compensation requires a baseline-normal factorial block of that change before interpreting failed protection. An independently validated nuclear-retention rescue, restoring functional nuclear TDP-43 to endogenous levels without repairing import, should protect axons and survival, testing mediation.

Discrimination. Cross NUP98 manipulation with verified stress-granule and persistent-TDP-43-assembly suppression. An intrinsic lesion predicts an early NUP98-dependent defect despite absent assemblies; sequestration predicts assembly-dependent failure [S3,S4]. Compare wild-type and phospho-null nuclei across identical Ran/importin/energy titrations, measuring retained aggregates and transport factors. Factor replenishment alone is not decisive: it may compensate for pore-affinity changes, while retained assemblies may explain persistent defects. C9orf72 neurons provide a context comparator, without requiring shared dependence [S2].

Falsification. Define onset as two consecutive import-rate measurements below a pilot-derived corrected-control threshold; preregister biologically meaningful equivalence margins and power confirmation using pilot variance. Verified pre-onset phosphoblockade leaving import failure equivalent to mutant controls, with compensation excluded, falsifies initiation. Verified disease-matched phosphorylation without the early transport phenotype falsifies sufficiency. Normal p25/CDK5 activity despite detectable disease phosphorylation, with sensitive positive controls, rejects the stipulated kinase-activation route. Failure of verified functional nuclear-TDP-43 restoration to protect neurons rejects depletion as the proposed injury mediator.

Limitations. Negative phosphosite detection only lowers confidence: brief or low-occupancy marks may escape calibrated assays. Sensor perturbation, conditional replacement, compensation, and kinase recruitment require validation. Phosphorylation may be downstream of broader stress; human chronology cannot be inferred from iPSC timing or postmortem tissue. This restricted preclinical hypothesis establishes neither a universal ALS cause nor a treatment.

ranking.item: CDK5-dependent NUP98 phosphorylation initiates nuclear-import failure and axonal injury in TARDBP-mutant motor neurons

author: grok
critique: The distinctive mechanism remains underresolved: kinase and sites are unspecified, and altered 'pore affinity' does not explain both increased passive permeability and slower import. Specify a domain-level interaction prediction and a fixed TDP-43 perturbation.

Kinase recruitment or phosphatase blockade can alter other substrates; coincident NUP98 phosphorylation and transport failure therefore cannot establish NUP98-specific sufficiency. Compare identical kinase activation in wild-type versus phospho-null NUP98, with kinase-dead recruitment and wild-type rescue controls.

Requiring additional FG-nucleoporin perturbations whenever NUP98 blockade fails risks moving the falsification threshold. Predefine compensators and demonstrate that compensation is induced by NUP98 blockade; otherwise distinguish rejection of NUP98 necessity from support for a broader, redundant FG-phosphorylation hypothesis.

author: grok
critique: The initiating catalyst is a class-level placeholder: the hypothesis requires 'a proline-directed kinase' but none is nominated, and the only supporting external knowledge is mitotic CDK1-NUP98 phosphorylation from post-mitotic-inappropriate cells. Fix: nominate a concrete interphase-expressed kinase candidate with evidence of neuronal expression and NPC proximity, and pre-register the specific NUP98 residues to be tested before committing to allele-editing arms.

The target nucleoporin has no support anywhere in the packet: [S1] never names NUP98, and the FG-barrier and mitotic-phosphorylation premises are imported from outside the evidence and only relabeled as assumptions. Fix: add a gating experiment that first verifies endogenous NUP98 abundance, NPC position, and basal phosphorylation state in iPSC motor neurons and ALS tissue so the downstream necessity/sufficiency arms rest on a demonstrated target rather than an imported one.

The plan is decision-rule dense but operationally unquantified: coupled assays (pre-onset phospho-MS on enriched intact NPCs, endogenous allele replacement, inducible kinase recruitment, crossed stress-granule arm, C9orf72 replication) carry no sample sizes, effect-size thresholds, or go/no-go timing, so 'lowers confidence rather than settling it' applies to the whole design. Fix: stage the work so expensive arms are gated on a minimum pre-onset phosphopeptide occupancy and a minimum fold-change in NLS import kinetics, then run contingency arms only if thresholds are met.

author: gpt
critique: The calcium–calpain–p25 trigger, the claim that NUP98 phosphorylation raises passive permeability, and axonal death as the injury readout sit in the hypothesis while the assumption list names only linkage, substrate identity, and phosphosites. Add those three steps to the speculative-bridge list, and state the calcium stimulus, the p25:p35 and CDK5 thresholds, and the required lead time before the first failed import measurement.

Residue identity is deferred, yet falsification is written as if a single mapped mark already exists. Pre-commit candidate CDK5 sites on pore-incorporated NUP98, or insert an explicit mapping stop-rule, so phospho-null replacement, recruitment sufficiency, and equivalence margins all refer to one frozen modification.

The live phosphosite sensor and the nuclear-retention rescue that restores TDP-43 without repairing import are undeveloped methods placed at the decision point. Use NLS-reporter import rates, size-selective passive leak, NPC-enriched phosphoproteomics, and genetic CDK5 or cleavage-resistant p35 alleles as the primary falsifiers, and treat the new tools as secondary checks after they are shown to leave baseline transport intact.

author: gpt
critique: The causal chain stacks two speculative layers: an already-assumed substrate (NUP98 phosphorylation) on top of an entirely unverified upstream arm (calcium→calpain→p35-to-p25→CDK5) for which the packet supplies no ALS evidence. If either upstream premise fails, the whole test pipeline collapses before the nucleoporin-phosphorylation question is evaluated. Fix: insert a cheap preliminary phase demonstrating disease-stage calcium/calpain/CDK5-p25 activation in TARDBP M337V versus isogenic-corrected neurons, or run kinase-agnostic phospho-mapping first with kinase assignment second, so falsifying the stipulated kinase route does not discard the phosphorylation hypothesis itself.

The biophysical claim that NUP98 phosphorylation simultaneously increases passive permeability and slows selective import is asserted, not derived: selective import depends substantially on the FG contributions of NUP62/NUP153/NUP358, yet the proposal only monitors those as compensatory changes rather than deriving how a NUP98-specific mark slows karyopherin-mediated transport. Fix: pre-specify the expected biophysics (e.g., phosphorylation weakening the barrier-conforming FG state versus altering karyopherin docking) and validate the dual transport effect in a reduced system (purified NPCs or reconstituted nuclear envelopes with phospho-null/phosphomimetic NUP98) before committing to the full iPSC longitudinal pipeline.

The mediation test assumes an 'independently validated nuclear-retention rescue restoring nuclear TDP-43 without repairing import' exists and is clean, but if such a rescue works by reducing cytoplasmic aggregation or stress, it could secondarily lower calcium/calpain/CDK5 activation and therefore phosphorylation, confounding the inference that nuclear TDP-43 depletion specifically mediates axonal injury. Fix: require re-measurement of phosphorylation occupancy, permeability, and import kinetics after rescue (plus direct cytoplasmic-assembly and calcium-stress readouts), so protection with demonstrably unperturbed pore phosphorylation is the only accepted mediation result.
